description: We are SkyPioneers, a results-driven team dedicated to turning bold ambitions into tangible reality. While we embrace forward-thinking innovation, we define ourselves not merely by the scale of our ideas, but by the discipline, resilience, and consistent effort required to bring them to life. We are not just dreamers—we are builders and doers who bridge the gap between vision and achievement through relentless execution and collaboration.
summary:
With SkyPioneers members, we created a website that explores this overlooked side of space exploration. It takes a closer look to three scientific instruments left on the Moon and Mars, explaining their purposes, their contributions, and the stories behind them.
Our goal is to make people more aware of what remains after a mission and why these objects are still worth studying. By using NASA data, images, and clear visual storytelling, we want to make this information accessible and interesting to everyone.
details: Abandoned but not forgotten is a digital web or storytelling project that explores the stories and lasting legacies of three remarkable examples of NASA space exploration technology: the Lunar Roving Vehicles, the Ingenuity Mars Helicopter, and the Pioneer 10 and 11 spacecraft. Through a visually engaging presentation, our project explains what these machines were designed to do, how they contributed to space exploration, what happened to them after their missions, and why their achievements still matter today. By combining reliable NASA research, historical images, key statistics, timelines, and visual comparisons, we transform complex scientific information into an accessible and engaging story. The project aims to raise awareness about the importance of space exploration, inspire curiosity about science and technology, and show that even when a mission ends, its discoveries and impact can live on. Our creative approach connects three different destinations—the Moon, Mars, and deep space—through one central theme: the legacy of human-made machines beyond their operational life. To develop the project, we used NASA's official websites and mission resources for research and fact-checking, along with Gemini to design and organize our web . Throughout the process, our team considered scientific accuracy, source reliability, clarity, visual quality, accessibility, and audience engagement. We also made sure to distinguish between equipment left on the Moon or Mars and spacecraft that continued travelling through deep space, keeping our storytelling both meaningful and scientifically accurate.
